	"shared/sdk/regenny/regenny/LTVisTree.hpp"
	"shared/sdk/regenny/regenny/LTVisTreeNode.hpp"
	"shared/sdk/regenny/regenny/LTWorldClientBSP.hpp"
	"shared/sdk/regenny/regenny/LTWorldModelObject.hpp"
	"shared/sdk/regenny/regenny/LTWorldTreeLink.hpp"
	"shared/sdk/regenny/regenny/LTWorldTreeNode.hpp"
	"shared/sdk/regenny/regenny/PlayerZoom.hpp"

)

# ---- NO OPENXR IN THE GAME ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#
# The mod contains no OpenXR code at all: the runtime, the loader, the instance and the session all
# live in the 64-bit host (tools/xr64), and the game talks to it purely over the shared mapping in
# shared/xr/SharedFrame.hpp. So nothing here ever loads openxr_loader.dll.
#
# The delete below is housekeeping for trees that built while an earlier attempt DID ship a 32-bit
# loader here. Dropping a copy rule does not remove what it already copied, and a leftover DLL in
# bin/ invites exactly the wrong conclusion about where OpenXR runs. Same class of trap as a stale
# CMake cache silently not compiling a new .cpp (AGENTS.md rule 10).
#
# Why that attempt was reverted, recorded because the numbers cost a session to get: shipping it
# moved the mod onto the Khronos loader, which loads fine under LAA and enumerates 89 extensions
# (against 35 direct, the difference being the implicit API layers the loader inserts) and then
# fails xrCreateInstance with XR_ERROR_FILE_ACCESS_ERROR (-32). A conformant path that cannot
# create an instance is worse than a less conformant one that can.
add_custom_command(TARGET fear2vr POST_BUILD
	COMMAND ${CMAKE_COMMAND} -E rm -f "$<TARGET_FILE_DIR:fear2vr>/openxr_loader.dll"
	VERBATIM)

unset(CMKR_TARGET)
unset(CMKR_SOURCES)

	set_property(DIRECTORY ${PROJECT_SOURCE_DIR} PROPERTY VS_STARTUP_PROJECT injector)

		"${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/bin"
	RUNTIME_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY_RELWITHDEBINFO
		"${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/bin"
	RUNTIME_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY_DEBUG
		"${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/bin"
)

# staging/ holds what the injector places next to the game (DXVK's d3d9.dll and its licence).
# Copy it beside injector.exe so the injector's own 'look next to me' lookup finds it -- one
# mechanism, no search paths. copy_directory_if_different is a no-op when nothing changed, so this
# does not dirty the output on every build.
add_custom_command(TARGET injector POST_BUILD
    COMMAND ${CMAKE_COMMAND} -E copy_directory_if_different
        "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/staging"
        "$<TARGET_FILE_DIR:injector>"
    COMMENT "Staging DXVK and its licence beside injector.exe"
    VERBATIM)

unset(CMKR_TARGET)
unset(CMKR_SOURCES)

add_test(
    NAME fixture-test
    COMMAND fixture-test
        --injector $<TARGET_FILE:injector>
        --dll      $<TARGET_FILE:fear2vr>
        --fixture  "W:/SteamLibrary/steamapps/common/FEAR2/FEAR2.exe"
        --port     8798
)
# 420s, not 180. The suite is ~85s, plus up to ~25s if it has to cold-start the game through
# `injector.exe --launch` (measured after resume_game.py stopped blind-sleeping; it used to be
# 165s). The suite grew a closed-loop aim director whose checks physically turn the player:
# driving the pitch into both clamps and back is several seconds each, and a checkpoint restore
# (only taken when the fixture is unusable) is ~15s on its own. Measured at ~90s healthy, and it
# timed out at 180 on a run that took the restore path -- a timeout reports as a failure with no
# output at all, which is the least diagnosable red there is.
set_tests_properties(fixture-test PROPERTIES SKIP_RETURN_CODE 77 TIMEOUT 420)

unset(CMKR_TARGET)
unset(CMKR_SOURCES)

# ---- PRINTF ARGUMENTS, CHECKED BY MACHINE ------------------------------------------------------
#
# The host's periodic log line broke three times in one session: arguments inserted where they read
# well in the source rather than where the format wanted them, a double printed through %llu, and a
# format field left behind after its argument was deleted -- which handed a float to %s and CRASHED
# THE HOST inside strnlen. MSVC does not warn at this project's level, and a 36-argument call
# cannot be checked by eye; I signed off on that one twice while it was wrong.
#
# Needs no build and no game, so it costs a fraction of a second on every ctest run.
#
# REGISTERED EITHER WAY. This used to be wrapped in `if(Python3_Interpreter_FOUND)`, so on a
# machine without Python the test simply CEASED TO EXIST -- ctest reported three passing targets
# and a mandatory check had silently left the suite. A check that can disappear is not mandatory,
# and "it passed" then means something different depending on the machine. When Python is missing
# the target is registered as a FAILING one that says why, which is loud, honest and fixable.
find_package(Python3 COMPONENTS Interpreter QUIET)
if(Python3_Interpreter_FOUND)
	add_test(NAME format-strings
		COMMAND ${Python3_EXECUTABLE} "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/tools/check_formats.py"
		WORKING_DIRECTORY "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}")
else()
	# FAILS WITH A REASON. `cmake -E false` would fail silently, which turns "mandatory check
	# absent" into "mandatory check red for no stated cause" -- barely an improvement. A one-line
	# script says what is missing and how to fix it, in the ctest output where someone will read it.
	file(WRITE "${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/format_strings_no_python.cmake"
		"message(FATAL_ERROR \"format-strings needs a Python 3 interpreter and CMake found none. Install Python 3 or put it on PATH; this check is not optional -- see tools/check_formats.py.\")\n")
	add_test(NAME format-strings
		COMMAND ${CMAKE_COMMAND} -P "${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/format_strings_no_python.cmake")
endif()
set_tests_properties(format-strings PROPERTIES TIMEOUT 60)

unset(CMKR_TARGET)
unset(CMKR_SOURCES)
